audits.text:
## 50e0af791608

**Reproduced lesson shortcut — wall-ignorant Manhattan geometry can fit all
visible demos and fail the query.** Generator SHA256
`b953acb9cdd719a06c76b65028d3c81af30b30914fbb81f1cba08c3d6df5da12`;
declared and normalized rule hash `f0c150157293`.

For medium seed 33 at sample index 0, the ordinary sequential lesson contains
three `vertical_corridor_pocket` demonstrations followed by a
`symmetric_block_horizontal` query. A rival that ignores walls and marks zeros
whose Manhattan distances to red and green sum to their direct Manhattan distance
matches all three Racket demonstration outputs, then disagrees with the query's
true union of maze shortest paths. All four inputs pass `self_check`, belong to
the documented domain, and the Python mirror matches Racket. Full grids, actual
Racket outputs, rival outputs, hashes, and reproduction command are in
`checks/audit-50e-manhattan-window.json`.

This is not isolated. Over medium seeds 0–999, sample indices 0–5, and cyclic
lesson starts 0, 1, and 2, the probe examined 6,000 draw records (3,449 unique
inputs) and 3,000 three-demo windows with zero validator failures. The rival fit
all three demos in 45 windows; in 32 of those, the next query refuted it. Exact
profiles and the first 20 witnesses are in `checks/audit-prevalence.json`.

Ordinary lint passes (`checks/audit-50e-lint/`), but semantic-gate fails because
the generator declares no strict/witness/lesson contract
(`checks/audit-50e-semantic/`). A schedule or lesson assembler should guarantee at
least one wall-sensitive witness in every exported demo window and declare this
Manhattan rival. No fix was made because this was an audit-only target.

triage.reason: Both source-bound audit reports retained. Target census counts remain reviewer-reported, not an independently rerun target battery. Targets left untouched.
